title: NASA electrostatics lab measures thrust in high vacuum

tellings.quote: We've been doing that since 2020. So, for the last 6 years, we test almost every day, probably every other day.

plain: A NASA electrostatics lab in Florida, near Kennedy Space Center, has been measuring thrust from electrically charged devices in high vacuum, testing "almost every day, probably every other day" since 2020. That is what the engineer Charles Buhler says, as someone who runs the tests, building on ideas from the inventor Thomas Townsend Brown. If true, it would point to a way of pushing a craft without burning fuel.
